candidates.title: Operando cobalt-state comparison under TEOA versus TEA
candidates.purpose: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA in the primary P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 CO2-photoreduction formulation changes observable cobalt oxidation-state, coordination, or stability signatures during operation, and whether any donor-dependent state difference tracks catalytic output.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 anchors the P01 TEOA-based CoCl2+bpy+g-C3N4 formulation and motivates TEA as a comparator within the same family. EV052, EV076, EV088, GX008, and EV068 support operando or near-operando XAS plus complementary UV-vis/Raman/IR style characterization as a way to monitor catalyst state during CO2 reduction rather than relying only on recovered samples. GX001, GX005, and GX011 justify testing whether donor identity could alter cobalt coordination/speciation, but these are transferred from other cobalt or bipyridine-related systems and do not establish the same chemistry here. EV085 cautions that donor decomposition or decomposition-derived catalysts can confound interpretation, so this proposal is limited to donor-dependent cobalt-linked observables and stability trends unless independent methods converge.

comparisons.inference: Primary single-variable test of whether donor identity changes cobalt-linked observables or stability trends under matched turnover conditions; any correlated product shift is associative rather than by itself causal proof.

Descriptive control for whether the TEOA formulation shows illumination-associated cobalt-state changes beyond dark-state coordination or hold-time effects; not a clean single-factor causal test because state handling also differs.
Descriptive control for whether the TEA formulation shows illumination-associated cobalt-state changes beyond dark-state donor interaction or hold-time effects; not a clean single-factor causal test.
Bounds non-cobalt backgrounds in the TEOA matrix so cobalt-linked features are not assigned from donor, ligand, support, or cell signals alone.
Bounds non-cobalt backgrounds in the TEA matrix so donor-specific interference is measured rather than assumed absent.
Descriptive comparison of donor-specific matrix backgrounds without cobalt; useful for interference assessment, not for cobalt-state causation.

procedure: Prepare one verified P01 baseline formulation, then generate TEOA and TEA variants by donor substitution only; separately prepare matched no-cobalt matrices for both donors and confirm identical reactor geometry, gas handling, and optical path.

Collect pre-illumination reference spectra for all groups, then acquire operando or near-operando Co-focused XAS and at least one complementary bulk method such as UV-vis during CO2 photoreaction for cobalt-containing groups; acquire matched background spectra for no-cobalt groups.
Run dark hold-time references for each donor and synchronize product sampling for CO and H2 with the spectroscopic runs where detection permits.

Interpret donor-dependent spectral evolution using only features justified by internal consistency and background subtraction; reserve species naming or mechanistic claims unless independent observables converge and no-cobalt matrices exclude donor-specific interference.
measurements: Co K-edge XANES features versus time, including edge-position and intensity changes if above matrix background
EXAFS-derived coordination-shell trends versus time, reported as model-dependent when multiple fits remain plausible
Complementary UV-vis spectral evolution of the reaction mixture or suspended system under matched sampling state
CO and H2 product amounts or rates from the same runs to test whether spectral differences track catalytic output
No-cobalt background spectra for both TEOA and TEA matrices to identify donor/support/cell contributions
Dark hold-time spectra for each donor as descriptive references rather than operating-state surrogates
candidates.supports: Support for H04 would be a reproducible donor-dependent difference between E19G01 and E19G02 in cobalt-linked operando or near-operando observables under otherwise matched conditions, with TEA and TEOA showing different spectral evolution trajectories, coordination trends, or decay patterns that align with different CO/H2 outputs, while the paired no-cobalt matrices do not account for the differences.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H04 would be that E19G01 and E19G02 show indistinguishable cobalt-linked spectral features and temporal evolution within method resolution, similar stability trends, and no donor-dependent divergence beyond matrix backgrounds, despite independently reproducible CO/H2 differences under the same matched conditions. That would weaken cobalt-speciation or cobalt-deactivation as the main explanation.
candidates.inconclusive: The result is inconclusive if cobalt signals are too weak, suspension/scattering prevents reliable extraction, donor substitution changes matrix background enough to obscure cobalt features even after no-cobalt controls, multiple cobalt-state models fit equally well, or product differences are not reproduced under the exact spectroscopic-cell conditions. A donor-dependent spectral change without product correlation remains descriptive only.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent numerical loadings or beam conditions. Use the literature-anchored P01 composition only after source verification. Pilot first to choose the lowest cobalt concentration and path length that still give reproducible cobalt-edge signal above both donor-matrix backgrounds while preserving measurable CO/H2 formation in the spectroscopic cell. Match donor formulations by the same verified baseline recipe except donor identity. Calibrate illumination by equal reactor geometry and measured incident photon flux at the sample. If true operando XAS is impractical, downgrade to near-operando rapid-transfer sampling with the same groups and explicitly narrow inference to time-adjacent, not strictly operating-state, observations.
candidates.limitations: The active cobalt species in P01 is unresolved, and support-associated, solution-phase, and decomposition-derived cobalt species may coexist. Operando XAS is element-specific but cannot by itself prove the catalytic intermediate, isolate donor photochemistry as upstream cause, or exclude decomposition pathways. Complementary UV-vis changes are non-unique and may reflect donor, ligand, support, or scattering effects. Dark comparisons here remain descriptive because irradiation and sampling_mode both differ. Even with paired no-cobalt matrices, assignment should stop at donor-dependent cobalt-linked observables unless independent methods support a narrower claim.

candidates.title: Operando IR/EPR donor-adduct screen
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA versus TEOA causes different donor-associated cobalt or substrate-bound species under matched P01 conditions, while bounding what any spectral differences can and cannot establish about the CO/H2 shift.
candidates.source_to_proposal: GX011 suggests TEOA can form catalyst adduct-like species in a bipyridine carbonyl system, motivating a cautious transfer test for donor-specific adduct chemistry in Co-bpy rather than assuming the same species. EV016 shows EPR can detect TEOA-derived radicals and that TEA/TEOA can differ in line shape because of physical properties, supporting donor-comparative EPR with matched blanks. EV068 supports operando FTIR/EPR to follow working-state interactions instead of recovered samples only. EV085 warns that donor decomposition and decomposition-derived active species can confound assignments, so symmetric donor-specific blanks are required and any signal must be treated as descriptive unless tied to matched catalytic outputs.

comparisons.inference: Primary donor-identity comparison. Reproducible donor-specific IR bands or EPR features under otherwise matched conditions would support a cobalt-speciation or donor-adduct contribution, but not by itself prove causality for CO/H2.

Tests whether TEOA-dependent features require donor presence. Features absent without donor are consistent with donor-derived radicals, donor binding, or donor-enabled substrate intermediates, but remain assignment-limited.
Tests whether TEA-dependent features require donor presence under the same matched framework, preventing asymmetry in donor interpretation.
Screens whether candidate TEOA features require cobalt. Signals present in both groups are background from donor, support, solvent, or CO2 handling rather than cobalt-specific species.
Screens whether candidate TEA features require cobalt. This symmetric control is needed because TEA and TEOA can differ in donor-radical and physical-property backgrounds.

Tests whether candidate TEOA-associated features are light-generated. A light-only appearance supports turnover-related or photogenerated species; persistence in dark suggests pre-equilibrium binding or background chemistry.
Tests whether candidate TEA-associated features are light-generated under matched donor-specific conditions.

procedure: Prepare matched baseline-family mixtures using the verified P01 component identities; keep vessel geometry, gas handling, solvent ratio, and sampling timing identical across groups.

Run a short pilot to choose concentration and optical path windows that avoid detector saturation and give measurable cobalt-region EPR/IR baselines; lock those settings before the TEA versus TEOA comparison.
Collect dark/background spectra first, then acquire operando or rapid sealed near-operando IR and EPR data under CO2 during illumination for each group using the same time points.

Pair the spectral campaign with matched product analysis from the same batches or parallel identically prepared batches so spectral differences can be compared with CO and H2 outputs without assuming causation.
Use replicate preparations and conservative peak assignment rules, reporting unmatched or ambiguous features as unknown signals rather than named intermediates.
measurements: In situ or near-operando IR difference spectra under CO2 and illumination, tracking donor-dependent new bands, band shifts, and growth or decay behavior relative to dark and donor-free baselines.
In situ or rapid-freeze or rapid-transfer EPR spectra, tracking appearance, disappearance, g-pattern changes, and line broadening under TEA versus TEOA conditions.
Matched catalytic readouts from parallel or same-batch experiments: CO and H2 amounts or rates, reported together rather than selectivity alone.
Background spectra from donor-free, no-cobalt, and dark controls for both donors to establish which signals are not cobalt-specific or not light-dependent.
If signal strength allows, time ordering of spectral changes relative to product formation; this can show correlation but cannot by itself identify the sole active species.
candidates.supports: H04 is supported if, under the locked matched P01 comparison, TEA and TEOA show reproducibly different cobalt-requiring and light-dependent IR and or EPR signatures, or different persistence or loss of such signatures over time, and those differences track a donor-dependent CO/H2 change better than donor-free, no-cobalt, or dark backgrounds do.
candidates.refutes: H04 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give no reproducible difference in cobalt-requiring, light-dependent IR/EPR observables within detection limits while catalytic CO/H2 still differs under the same matched conditions, favoring explanations upstream in donor photochemistry or downstream in proton or CO2 handling rather than cobalt-state divergence.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if spectra are too weak, dominated by background or support signals, changed by viscosity or other physical effects without cobalt specificity, or if donor-dependent signals appear but cannot be distinguished from donor decomposition, generic radical formation, or unsupported assignments. Correlation without clean symmetric controls also remains inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-backed P01 formulation family only for component identity, not exact invented numbers. First verify the baseline recipe from source records. Then run pilots to set sample concentration, path length, irradiation interval, and EPR acquisition mode by the rule that cobalt-containing samples must show stable unsaturated baselines and donor-free and no-cobalt controls must remain interpretable. If TEA and TEOA differ strongly in viscosity or optical density, adjust only the measurement configuration, not the chemical formulation, and document that this preserves matched chemistry while changing detection settings. Choose time points by a calibration run that captures pre-illumination, early illumination, and a later turnover window without exhausting the sample.
candidates.limitations: Assignments are transferred from nonidentical systems and may not map to Co-bpy. IR/EPR can reveal donor-dependent species or state changes but cannot alone establish the full catalytic mechanism, the exact structure of the active cobalt species, or product origin. TEA/TEOA physical-property differences can alter line shape and transport, so apparent spectral differences are not automatically chemical. Near-operando aliquots may miss the true instantaneous working state. No-cobalt controls are background screens, not full single-factor catalytic comparisons because total composition changes.

candidates.title: Single-omission matrix for donor-linked cobalt-state effects
candidates.purpose: Test whether any TEA-versus-TEOA difference in cobalt-state observables and CO/H2 distribution requires the full CoCl2+bpy+g-C3N4 assembly, using explicit one-factor omissions and bounded background interpretation.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 supports the CoCl2+bpy+g-C3N4+TEOA formulation family in MeCN/H2O and motivates this as the closest source-anchored platform for donor comparison. GX008 supports explicit negative controls and paired characterization plus product analysis. EV081 shows that partial or no-catalyst systems can still produce CO and H2, so omission results must be treated as necessity/background tests rather than proof of mechanism. GX016 supports the transferable idea that cobalt-centered identity can shift product selectivity under TEOA photocatalysis, motivating tests of whether donor-linked effects persist or collapse when ligand or support is removed. The proposal transfers these observations into a controlled omission matrix in the P01-style system; it does not assume literature-established active-species identity or that omitted formulations are mechanistic continuations of the full catalyst.

comparisons.inference: Primary donor-substitution benchmark in the full assembly. A reproducible difference here is required before omission results can localize where donor-linked divergence appears.

Tests whether donor-linked differences persist when bpy is omitted. Persistence would show that a full Co-bpy assembly is not required for the observed donor dependence; disappearance would indicate ligand-context dependence.

Tests whether donor-linked differences persist when g-C3N4 is omitted. Persistence would show that support association is not required for the observed donor dependence; disappearance would indicate support-context dependence.
Necessity test for bpy under TEOA. Any major loss or change indicates dependence on ligand presence, but this comparison alone does not establish why donor effects arise.
Necessity test for bpy under TEA, providing a matched counterpart to the TEOA ligand-omission comparison.
Necessity test for g-C3N4 under TEOA. Any major change indicates support dependence, but omitted systems may involve qualitatively different cobalt chemistry.
Necessity test for g-C3N4 under TEA, providing a matched counterpart to the TEOA support-omission comparison.

procedure: Verify the source-anchored P01 baseline composition from EV059, then prepare all six formulations so only the stated factor differs between compared groups.

Run a pilot to set concentration, path length, sampling times, and reactor loading that give detectable cobalt-state signal and measurable CO and H2 without detector saturation or severe bulk conversion.
For each group, collect pre-illumination and near-operando cobalt-state measurements under CO2 and matched illumination, then quantify CO and H2 from the same reaction workflow.

Compare donor effects within each assembly state first, then compare omission versus full-assembly groups within each donor while treating omissions as necessity tests rather than mechanistic identity tests.
Interpret any product in omission groups against matched blanks and analytical backgrounds; do not infer a single active species from one spectroscopic signature or recovered samples alone.
measurements: CO and H2 quantified together by one matched GC workflow for all groups, reporting amount and CO/H2 distribution.

A cobalt-state observable from an element- or coordination-sensitive method feasible in the laboratory context, such as operando or near-operando XAS, XPS-compatible sampling, or UV-Vis features, with sample state stated explicitly.
Change in cobalt-related spectral features or signal intensity from pre-illumination to illuminated CO2 conditions as a bounded indicator of donor-linked state change or deactivation.
Background product formation in omission groups, used to bound non-full-assembly contributions rather than to claim catalytic equivalence.
candidates.supports: H04 is supported if the full assembly shows a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in cobalt-state observables or stability trends and that donor-linked difference weakens, disappears, or changes character in at least one omission pair, indicating dependence on ligand or support context. Stronger support occurs if the direction of cobalt-state differences tracks the direction of CO/H2 changes across matched pairs.
candidates.refutes: H04 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give indistinguishable cobalt-state and stability observables in the full assembly within method resolution, and the ligand-omission and support-omission donor pairs likewise show no reproducible donor-linked divergence despite measurable products. It is further weakened if donor substitution changes CO/H2 but cobalt-state observables remain unchanged across all matched formulations.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if product signals are near background, cobalt-state signals are below detection or assignment is non-unique, omission causes optical or compositional changes that prevent comparable measurements, or session-to-session drift obscures donor-pair comparisons. A change seen in only one method without corroboration remains provisional.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations, catalyst loadings, or illumination settings. Use the verified EV059-style baseline for starting composition, then perform a pilot to choose the lowest concentration and path length that still provide stable cobalt-state signal above blanks and measurable CO and H2 above analytical detection. Choose an early sampling window before heavy conversion or visible precipitation. If support omission changes turbidity or absorbance, recalibrate acquisition settings with blanks while keeping reactor geometry, gas handling, and timing identical across compared groups.
candidates.limitations: Omission of bpy or g-C3N4 may generate qualitatively different cobalt species rather than partial versions of the full catalyst, so these are dependence tests, not continuity proofs. EV059 does not provide a direct TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in one frozen recipe, so baseline comparability still requires verification. Recovered-sample measurements may miss the operating state, and generic spectral changes cannot by themselves identify the active species or exact coordination geometry.
